newsitem.title: UK: Rentokil sees no major acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Rentokil sees no major acquisitions.

text.p: Rentokil Initial Plc chief executive Sir Clive Thompson said on Wednesday he did not expect the company to make any major acquisitions for the next two years while it integrated the BET operations bought last year.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television Thompson said there were 52 different BET businesses to be integrated into Rentokil Inital.
"I'd be very suprised to see us making major acquisitons for certainly under two years, and if we were to do so it would indicate that we had integrated the businesses extremely well," Thompson said.

However, Thompson said there were opportunities for "bolt-on acquisitions" in the core businesses of hygiene and cleaning, pest control and security "and I hope we'd be making those sorts of acquisitons."
Thompson said he expected to make a number of low-key disposals of BET operations over the next year.
"In the short term you'd expect to see a series, quite a number, of relatively small-sized disposals. In total terms over the next 12 months it might approach 50 to 100 million (stg)," he said.
Thompson said he intended to keep the bulk of BET's plant hire businesses in the medium term.
"Certainly for the medium term if not for the long term we are happy to keep the plant hire businesess, particularly in the U.S, and the main activities in the UK," he said.
Thompson said the company stood by its aim of doubling profit margins at BET, which he said were currently around seven percent after interest payemnts.

"We feel relatively confident that over the next two to three years we should be able to double those margins," he said, and added that there were still opportunities to improve margins, currently "in the mid-twenties," at the core Rentokil businesses.
